included: Designed around Portugal buyer use cases
warranty: General legal guidance: movable goods have a 3-year guarantee.
Where treated as immovable property, Portuguese law may provide 5 years generally and 10 years for structural construction elements.
Final warranty period, exclusions, maintenance duties and handover documents must be confirmed in the contract.
scopeFactors: Narrow roads, slopes, crane access and unloading space can change feasibility and cost.
Groundworks are site-specific and should not be hidden inside a vague house price.
Water, wastewater, power and internet assumptions need to be separated from the home itself.
Exterior, kitchen, terrace and energy choices should be limited enough to stay controllable.
Delivery route, timing and responsibility split need confirmation before commitment.
Residential, guest, work or rental use can change what needs to be checked locally.
riskChecks: Delivery access is often the first real constraint, especially in rural or hillside locations.
Supports and groundworks must be clearly scoped before the house is produced.
No page should promise installation or rental use without local checks.
How will it perform in summer?
Shade, orientation, ventilation and insulation strategy matter in Portuguese summer heat.
Transport, crane, services and landscaping assumptions need to be visible, not discovered late.
Engineering, energy and material claims should be backed by proper product documentation.
climatePoints: Orientation, shading, ventilation and insulation have to work together.
Materials and exterior detailing need to suit sun, wind and saltier air.
A home that sits empty part of the year still needs moisture and comfort thinking.
Deck, glazing and threshold details should make outside space feel like part of the home.
faq: Can I customise the tiny home?
Yes, but the first offer is intentionally limited. The goal is a controlled product, not an open-ended custom build.
Can this be installed anywhere in Portugal?
Location, access, land conditions, services, and permissions need to be checked before any commitment. Algarve enquiries are the first launch focus.
No final pricing claim is made on this page. Budget ranges are used to qualify the enquiry.
What makes HOMIE different from a cheap chalet?
HOMIE is positioned around timber construction, airtightness, insulation priorities, useful built-in functions, and a controlled options process.
Do I need land before contacting you?
No, but land status changes the conversation. If you already have land, access, services, and local constraints can be checked earlier.
Can HOMIE be used as a rental unit?
Possible rental use needs separate legal, planning, licensing, insurance, and financial checks. This page does not promise rental income.
What is included in the first model?
The first model is based on one bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, and compact living functions. Final inclusions should be confirmed in the brochure and scope.
Secondary enquiries outside Portugal can be qualified, but logistics, compliance, delivery, and local requirements need checking before any commitment.
